args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), the service failed health checks with an error rate of ~18%. v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy and the error rate is ~0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression, and find out why a release that was unhealthy in staging was promoted to production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

- **Rollback:** The broken release was v2.3.1, which had an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. us-east, us-west and eu-west are all now running v2.3.0, and the error rate is down to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) is open, and opening it paged the on-call engineer. It describes the failure, the rollback and the recovery.

v2.3.1 was already unhealthy in staging (as v2.3.1-rc) but still went to production. I listed two follow-ups in the incident: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and find out why a release that failed in staging was promoted.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
